title: E0040: Return Contract Violation
plain_english: Reports return values that contradict a declared return contract.
why_matters: A return value that violates a native type or PHPDoc `@return` contract can cause runtime type errors or break callers that rely on the documented contract. This rule uses Phanalist's bounded formal verification engine (Z3-backed) to detect feasible violating paths.
bad_example:
<?php
/** @return int */
function countItems(array $items): int
{
    return $items; // wrong return type
}
good_example:
<?php
/** @return int */
function countItems(array $items): int
{
    return count($items);
}
what_it_checks: Native return types and PHPDoc `@return` contracts
Missing return values on paths that must return a value
`never` contracts that make following code unreachable
Strict and weak PHP return coercion rules
Numeric, string, list, non-empty, and shaped array contracts
Generator returns are not checked against the generator return type
